newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch shares end flat after directionless day.
newsitem.headline: Dutch shares end flat after directionless day.

text.p: Dutch shares ended flat on Monday after a day of small swings in generally directionless trade, dealers said.
"There is no real news in the market and with none coming in during the day there was nothing much to go on," one trader said.
Oil major Royal Dutch was a loser again, dropping a further 4.40 guilders as the slide started by disappointing third quarter results last week was extended.
"It's been due a correction," the trader said.
Airline KLM was stable ahead of first-half results due on Tuesday and expected to be fairly disappointing.
"The share has traded down quite a lot recently in anticipation and maybe the bad news is already in the price," one dealer said.
KLM shares gained 0.50 guilders to finish at 41.90.

Retailer Ahold showed some strength into the close after the announcement of a major joint venture in Brazil late in the trading day. Ahold is to acquire 50 percent of Bompreco, Brazil's fourth-largest food retailer.
"It's a surprising and daring move," one analyst said. "With this step, Ahold has gained a foothold in Latin America's biggest and most developed market."
Ahold shares gained 1.40 guilders to finish at 101.20.
Dutch Telecoms operators KPN got a small boost from the BT/MCI mega-merger, adding 0.50 guilders to 63.00.
Its options were the most traded contract on the European Options Exchange, with calls beating puts by around 10,000 to 2,000 as investors looked for a cheap way onto the Telcoms bandwagon.
The market would likely continue to be quiet on Tuesday under the shadow of the U.S. ballot box, dealers said.
